items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 7:36PM PST until November 15 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet with sets 8 to 10 feet along west-facing beaches.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected, particularly along west-facing beaches where surf
will be highest.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adjusted high tides will be near 6.2-6.5
feet around midday on Saturday, which will combine with high
surf to produce minor coastal flooding. Highest surf is expected
to occur late Saturday into early Sunday. Surf begins to wane
Sunday afternoon but will remain elevated into Monday.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 13 at 7:35PM PST until November 14 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Seas 5 to 9 ft and west winds 20 to 25 knots will lead
to choppy seas and dangerous boating conditions.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from San Mateo Point to the Mexican
Border and out to 10 nm and Waters from San Mateo Point to the
Mexican Border Extending 10 to 60 nm out including San
Clemente Island.

* WHEN...From 10 AM today to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strongest winds will occur tonight until
10 AM Saturday. Seas and winds will begin to diminish Saturday
afternoon, but seas may remain above 7 feet into early Sunday,
especially south of San Clemente Island.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
